passages.text: Now Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were saying, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was living with Laban.
Laban was his father-in-law.
Jacob became very wealthy.
He had many flocks and servants.
Laban’s sons spoke among themselves.
They said, “Jacob has taken everything that belonged to our father.”
They said, “Jacob gained all this wealth from what was our father’s.”
Jacob heard what Laban’s sons were saying.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֤י בְנֵֽי־ לָבָן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָקַ֣ח יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֵ֖ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֑ינוּ וּמֵאֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔ינוּ עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַכָּבֹ֖ד הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And Jacob saw from the countenance of Laban that his attitude toward him had changed.
passages.sermon:
Jacob looked at Laban’s face.
Jacob saw Laban’s expression.
Laban did not look at Jacob as he did before.
Laban’s attitude toward Jacob had changed.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥רְא יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י לָבָ֑ן וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵינֶ֛נּוּ עִמּ֖וֹ כִּתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Jacob, “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jacob.
The LORD told Jacob to return to his homeland.
The LORD told Jacob to go back to the land of his fathers.
The LORD told Jacob to return to his relatives.
The LORD promised to be with Jacob.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹ֔ב שׁ֛וּב אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ אֲבוֹתֶ֖יךָ וּלְמוֹלַדְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאֶֽהְיֶ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flocks were, and he told them, “I can see from your father’s countenance that his attitude toward me has changed; but the God of my father has been with me.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
Jacob sent a message to Rachel and Leah.
Rachel and Leah were his wives.
Jacob called Rachel and Leah to the field.
Jacob kept his flocks in that field.
Jacob spoke to Rachel and Leah.
Jacob said, “I see your father’s face.
Your father is Laban.
Laban’s attitude toward me has changed.
He is not toward me as he was before.
But the God of my father has been with me.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיִּקְרָ֖א לְרָחֵ֣ל וּלְלֵאָ֑ה הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה אֶל־ צֹאנֽוֹ׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ן רֹאֶ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י אֲבִיכֶ֔ן כִּֽי־ אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אֵלַ֖י כִּתְמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֑ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֔י הָיָ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: You know that I have served your father with all my strength.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Rachel and Leah.
Jacob said, “You know this.”
I served your father.
I worked with all my strength.
passages.original: וְאַתֵּ֖נָה יְדַעְתֶּ֑ן כִּ֚י בְּכָל־ כֹּחִ֔י עָבַ֖דְתִּי אֶת־ אֲבִיכֶֽן׃

passages.text: And although he has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, God has not allowed him to harm me.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Rachel and Leah.
Jacob said that their father had deceived him.
Their father had changed Jacob’s wages ten times.
God did not let their father harm Jacob.
passages.original: וַאֲבִיכֶן֙ הֵ֣תֶל בִּ֔י וְהֶחֱלִ֥ף אֶת־ מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּ֖י עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת מֹנִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־ נְתָנ֣וֹ אֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהָרַ֖ע עִמָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore speckled offspring. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore streaked offspring.
passages.sermon:
Jacob is the speaker.
Jacob worked for Laban, his father-in-law.
Laban changed Jacob’s wages many times.
Laban sometimes said, “The speckled animals will be your wages.”
When Laban said this, all the flock gave birth to speckled animals.
Other times, Laban said, “The streaked animals will be your wages.”
When Laban said this, all the flock gave birth to streaked animals.
passages.original: אִם־ כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֗ר נְקֻדִּים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׂכָרֶ֔ךָ וְיָלְד֥וּ כָל־ הַצֹּ֖אן נְקֻדִּ֑ים וְאִם־ כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֗ר עֲקֻדִּים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׂכָרֶ֔ךָ וְיָלְד֥וּ כָל־ הַצֹּ֖אן עֲקֻדִּֽים׃

passages.text: Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.
passages.sermon: God acted with power.\r\nGod took your father's livestock.\r\nGod gave the livestock to me.
passages.original: וַיַּצֵּ֧ל אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־ מִקְנֵ֥ה אֲבִיכֶ֖ם וַיִּתֶּן־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: When the flocks were breeding, I saw in a dream that the streaked, spotted, and speckled males were mating with the females.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was watching the flocks.
The flocks were breeding.
Jacob looked up.
Jacob saw a dream.
In the dream, male goats were mating with the females.
These males were streaked, spotted, and speckled.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֵת֙ יַחֵ֣ם הַצֹּ֔אן וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֛י וָאֵ֖רֶא בַּחֲל֑וֹם וְהִנֵּ֤ה הָֽעַתֻּדִים֙ הָעֹלִ֣ים עַל־ הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּבְרֻדִּֽים׃

passages.text: In that dream the angel of God said to me, ‘Jacob!’ And I replied, ‘Here I am.’
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and Rebekah.
Jacob was living with Laban, his father-in-law.
God spoke to Jacob in a dream.
The angel of God appeared to Jacob in the dream.
The angel called Jacob by name.
The angel said, “Jacob!”
Jacob answered the angel.
Jacob said, “Here I am.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י מַלְאַ֧ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים בַּחֲל֖וֹם יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: ‘Look up,’ he said, ‘and see that all the males that are mating with the flock are streaked, spotted, or speckled; for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.
passages.sermon:
The angel of God spoke to Jacob in a dream.
The angel said, "Look up."
"See all the male goats that are mating with the flock."
"These males are streaked, spotted, or speckled."
"I have seen everything that Laban has done to you."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שָׂא־ נָ֨א עֵינֶ֤יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ כָּל־ הָֽעַתֻּדִים֙ הָעֹלִ֣ים עַל־ הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּבְרֻדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י רָאִ֔יתִי אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָבָ֖ן עֹ֥שֶׂה לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the pillar and made a solemn vow to Me. Now get up and leave this land at once, and return to your native land.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jacob in a dream.
God identified Himself clearly.
God said, “I am the God of Bethel.
You anointed a pillar for Me at Bethel.
You made a solemn vow to Me there.
Now get up.
Leave this land immediately.
Return to the land where you were born.”
passages.original: אָנֹכִ֤י הָאֵל֙ בֵּֽית־ אֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָשַׁ֤חְתָּ שָּׁם֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָדַ֥רְתָּ לִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם נֶ֑דֶר עַתָּ֗ה ק֥וּם צֵא֙ מִן־ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְשׁ֖וּב אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: And Rachel and Leah replied, “Do we have any portion or inheritance left in our father’s house?
passages.sermon:
Rachel and Leah were Jacob’s wives.
Rachel and Leah spoke to Jacob.
Rachel and Leah asked Jacob a question.
They said, “Do we have any share left in our father’s house?”
They said, “Do we have any inheritance there?”
passages.original: וַתַּ֤עַן רָחֵל֙ וְלֵאָ֔ה וַתֹּאמַ֖רְנָה ל֑וֹ הַע֥וֹד לָ֛נוּ חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Are we not regarded by him as outsiders? Not only has he sold us, but he has certainly squandered what was paid for us.
passages.sermon:
Rachel and Leah spoke about their father Laban.
Laban is their father.
Rachel and Leah said, “He treats us as outsiders.
He sold us.
He used up all the money he received for us.”
passages.original: הֲל֧וֹא נָכְרִיּ֛וֹת נֶחְשַׁ֥בְנוּ ל֖וֹ כִּ֣י מְכָרָ֑נוּ וַיֹּ֥אכַל גַּם־ אָכ֖וֹל אֶת־ כַּסְפֵּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Surely all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children. So do whatever God has told you.”
passages.sermon:
Rachel and Leah spoke to Jacob.
Rachel and Leah are Jacob’s wives.
Rachel and Leah said that God took wealth from their father Laban.
This wealth now belongs to Rachel, Leah, and their children.
Rachel and Leah told Jacob to do everything God commanded him.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כָל־ הָעֹ֗שֶׁר אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּ֤יל אֱלֹהִים֙ מֵֽאָבִ֔ינוּ לָ֥נוּ ה֖וּא וּלְבָנֵ֑ינוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֵלֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵֽׂה׃

passages.text: Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on camels, and he drove all his livestock before him, along with all the possessions he had acquired in Paddan-aram, to go to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac.
Jacob lived in Paddan-aram.
Jacob got up.
He put his children on camels.
He put his wives on camels.
He gathered all his livestock.
He took all his possessions.
He had acquired these possessions in Paddan-aram.
Jacob set out to go to Canaan.
He went to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.
passages.original: וַיָּ֖קָם יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיִּשָּׂ֛א אֶת־ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶת־ נָשָׁ֖יו עַל־ הַגְּמַלִּֽים׃ וַיִּנְהַ֣ג אֶת־ כָּל־ מִקְנֵ֗הוּ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ רְכֻשׁוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָכָ֔שׁ מִקְנֵה֙ קִנְיָנ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָכַ֖שׁ בְּפַדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם לָב֛וֹא אֶל־ יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו אַ֥רְצָה כְּנָֽעַן׃

passages.text: Now while Laban was out shearing his sheep, Rachel stole her father’s household idols.
passages.sermon:
Laban was Rachel’s father.
Laban went out to shear his sheep.
Rachel took her father’s household idols.
Rachel stole these idols while Laban was away.
passages.original: וְלָבָ֣ן הָלַ֔ךְ לִגְזֹ֖ז אֶת־ צֹאנ֑וֹ וַתִּגְנֹ֣ב רָחֵ֔ל אֶת־ הַתְּרָפִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאָבִֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Moreover, Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac.
Laban was an Aramean.
Jacob deceived Laban.
Jacob did not tell Laban that he was running away.
passages.original: וַיִּגְנֹ֣ב יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶת־ לֵ֥ב לָבָ֖ן הָאֲרַמִּ֑י עַל־ בְּלִי֙ הִגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י בֹרֵ֖חַ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: So he fled with all his possessions, crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son-in-law of Laban.
Jacob took everything he owned.
Jacob ran away.
Jacob got up.
Jacob crossed the Euphrates River.
Jacob set out toward the hill country of Gilead.
passages.original: וַיִּבְרַ֥ח הוּא֙ וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֔וֹ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר אֶת־ הַנָּהָ֑ר וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־ פָּנָ֖יו הַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: On the third day Laban was informed that Jacob had fled.
passages.sermon:
Laban was an Aramean.
Jacob was his relative.
Jacob fled from Laban.
Three days passed.
Someone told Laban that Jacob had fled.
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְלָבָ֖ן בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: So he took his relatives with him, pursued Jacob for seven days, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.
passages.sermon:
Laban was Jacob’s father-in-law.
Laban took his relatives with him.
Laban pursued Jacob.
Laban chased Jacob for seven days.
Laban overtook Jacob in the hill country of Gilead.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־ אֶחָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף אַחֲרָ֔יו דֶּ֖רֶךְ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיַּדְבֵּ֥ק אֹת֖וֹ בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: But that night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream and warned him, “Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.”
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord of all.
Laban is an Aramean man.
That night, God came to Laban in a dream.
God spoke to Laban.
God warned Laban.
God said, “Be careful.”
God said, “Do not say anything to Jacob.”
God said, “Do not say anything good or bad to him.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־ לָבָ֥ן הָאֲרַמִּ֖י בַּחֲלֹ֣ם הַלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הִשָּׁ֧מֶר לְךָ֛ פֶּן־ תְּדַבֵּ֥ר עִֽם־ יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִטּ֥וֹב עַד־ רָֽע׃

passages.text: Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban overtook him, and Laban and his relatives camped there as well.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was in the hill country of Gilead.
Jacob set up his tent there.
Laban came and caught up to Jacob.
Laban was not alone.
Laban brought his relatives with him.
Laban and his relatives camped in the hill country of Gilead too.
passages.original: וַיַּשֵּׂ֥ג לָבָ֖ן אֶֽת־ יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיַעֲקֹ֗ב תָּקַ֤ע אֶֽת־ אָהֳלוֹ֙ בָּהָ֔ר וְלָבָ֛ן תָּקַ֥ע אֶת־ אֶחָ֖יו בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: Then Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done? You have deceived me and carried off my daughters like captives of war!
passages.sermon:
Laban was the father-in-law of Jacob.
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban said, "What have you done?"
Laban said, "You deceived me."
Laban said, "You took my daughters away."
Laban said, "You treated my daughters like captives taken in war."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ וַתִּגְנֹ֖ב אֶת־ לְבָבִ֑י וַתְּנַהֵג֙ אֶת־ בְּנֹתַ֔י כִּשְׁבֻי֖וֹת חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: Why did you run away secretly and deceive me, without even telling me? I would have sent you away with joy and singing, with tambourines and harps.
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban asked Jacob a question.
Laban said, "Why did you run away in secret?"
Laban said, "Why did you deceive me?"
Laban said, "You did not tell me you were leaving."
Laban said, "If you had told me, I would have sent you away with joy."
Laban said, "I would have sent you away with singing."
Laban said, "I would have sent you away with tambourines and harps."
passages.original: לָ֤מָּה נַחְבֵּ֙אתָ֙ לִבְרֹ֔חַ וַתִּגְנֹ֖ב אֹתִ֑י וְלֹא־ הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י וָֽאֲשַׁלֵּחֲךָ֛ בְּשִׂמְחָ֥ה וּבְשִׁרִ֖ים בְּתֹ֥ף וּבְכִנּֽוֹר׃

passages.text: But you did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. Now you have done a foolish thing.
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban is the father of Jacob’s wives.
Laban said, “You did not let me kiss my grandchildren goodbye.”
Laban said, “You did not let me kiss my daughters goodbye.”
Laban said, “You have acted foolishly.”
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א נְטַשְׁתַּ֔נִי לְנַשֵּׁ֥ק לְבָנַ֖י וְלִבְנֹתָ֑י עַתָּ֖ה הִסְכַּ֥לְתָּֽ עֲשֽׂוֹ׃

passages.text: I have power to do you great harm, but last night the God of your father said to me, ‘Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.’
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban had power to harm Jacob and his family.
Laban could have done them great evil.
But God spoke to Laban the night before.
God is the God of Jacob’s father.
God warned Laban.
God said, “Be careful not to speak to Jacob, either good or bad.”
Laban obeyed God’s warning.
passages.original: יֶשׁ־ לְאֵ֣ל יָדִ֔י לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עִמָּכֶ֖ם רָ֑ע וֵֽאלֹהֵ֨י אֲבִיכֶ֜ם אֶ֣מֶשׁ׀ אָמַ֧ר אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֗ר הִשָּׁ֧מֶר לְךָ֛ מִדַּבֵּ֥ר עִֽם־ יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִטּ֥וֹב עַד־ רָֽע׃

passages.text: Now you have gone off because you long for your father’s house. But why have you stolen my gods?”
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban said, “You left and went away.
You left because you missed your father’s house.
But you stole my gods.
Why did you steal my gods?”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ הָלֹ֣ךְ הָלַ֔כְתָּ כִּֽי־ נִכְסֹ֥ף נִכְסַ֖פְתָּה לְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ לָ֥מָּה גָנַ֖בְתָּ אֶת־ אֱלֹהָֽי׃

passages.text: “I was afraid,” Jacob answered, “for I thought you would take your daughters from me by force.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob answered Laban’s question.
Jacob said he was afraid.
Jacob feared Laban.
Jacob thought Laban might take his daughters away from him by force.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן יַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְלָבָ֑ן כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔אתִי כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן־ תִּגְזֹ֥ל אֶת־ בְּנוֹתֶ֖יךָ מֵעִמִּֽי׃

passages.text: If you find your gods with anyone here, he shall not live! In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself if anything is yours, and take it back.” For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
Jacob spoke to Laban, his father-in-law.
Jacob said, “If you find your gods with anyone here, that person will not live.
Our relatives are here as witnesses.
Look and see if you find anything that belongs to you among my things.
If you find something, take it back.”
Jacob did not know that Rachel, his wife, had stolen the idols.
passages.original: עִ֠ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֣א אֶת־ אֱלֹהֶיךָ֮ לֹ֣א יִֽחְיֶה֒ נֶ֣גֶד אַחֵ֧ינוּ הַֽכֶּר־ לְךָ֛ מָ֥ה עִמָּדִ֖י וְקַֽח־ לָ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־ יָדַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב כִּ֥י רָחֵ֖ל גְּנָבָֽתַם׃

passages.text: So Laban went into Jacob’s tent, then Leah’s tent, and then the tents of the two maidservants, but he found nothing. Then he left Leah’s tent and entered Rachel’s tent.
passages.sermon:
Laban searched for his household idols.
He went into Jacob’s tent.
He did not find the idols there.
He went into Leah’s tent.
He did not find the idols there.
He went into the tents of the two maidservants.
He did not find the idols there.
Laban left Leah’s tent.
He entered Rachel’s tent.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א לָבָ֜ן בְּאֹ֥הֶל יַעֲקֹ֣ב׀ וּבְאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֗ה וּבְאֹ֛הֶל שְׁתֵּ֥י הָאֲמָהֹ֖ת וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑א וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֵאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּאֹ֥הֶל רָחֵֽל׃

passages.text: Now Rachel had taken Laban’s household idols, put them in the saddlebag of her camel, and was sitting on them. And Laban searched everything in the tent but found nothing.
passages.sermon:
Rachel was the wife of Jacob.
Rachel took the household idols that belonged to Laban.
She put the idols in the saddlebag of her camel.
Rachel sat on the saddlebag.
Laban searched the entire tent.
Laban did not find the idols.
passages.original: וְרָחֵ֞ל לָקְחָ֣ה אֶת־ הַתְּרָפִ֗ים וַתְּשִׂמֵ֛ם בְּכַ֥ר הַגָּמָ֖ל וַתֵּ֣שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיְמַשֵּׁ֥שׁ לָבָ֛ן אֶת־ כָּל־ הָאֹ֖הֶל וְלֹ֥א מָצָֽא׃

passages.text: Rachel said to her father, “Sir, do not be angry that I cannot stand up before you; for I am having my period.” So Laban searched, but could not find the household idols.
passages.sermon:
Rachel spoke to her father Laban.
She said, “Sir, do not be angry with me.”
She said, “I cannot stand up before you.”
She said, “I am having my period.”
Laban searched the tent.
Laban did not find the household idols.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ אָבִ֗יהָ אַל־ יִ֙חַר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֣י ל֤וֹא אוּכַל֙ לָק֣וּם מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ כִּי־ דֶ֥רֶךְ נָשִׁ֖ים לִ֑י וַיְחַפֵּ֕שׂ וְלֹ֥א מָצָ֖א אֶת־ הַתְּרָפִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Jacob became incensed and challenged Laban. “What is my crime?” he said. “For what sin of mine have you so hotly pursued me?
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a servant of God.
Jacob became very angry.
Jacob argued with Laban.
Jacob spoke directly to Laban.
Jacob said, “What is my crime?”
Jacob said, “What is my sin?”
Jacob said, “Why have you chased after me so fiercely?”
passages.original: וַיִּ֥חַר לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיָּ֣רֶב בְּלָבָ֑ן וַיַּ֤עַן יַעֲקֹב֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְלָבָ֔ן מַה־ פִּשְׁעִי֙ מַ֣ה חַטָּאתִ֔י כִּ֥י דָלַ֖קְתָּ אַחֲרָֽי׃

passages.text: You have searched all my goods! Have you found anything that belongs to you? Put it here before my brothers and yours, that they may judge between the two of us.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob said, “You searched all my belongings.
You looked through everything I own.
Did you find anything that belongs to you?
If you found something of yours, put it here.
Place it in front of my relatives and your relatives.
Let them judge between us.
Let them decide who is right.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ מִשַּׁ֣שְׁתָּ אֶת־ כָּל־ כֵּלַ֗י מַה־ מָּצָ֙אתָ֙ מִכֹּ֣ל כְּלֵי־ בֵיתֶ֔ךָ שִׂ֣ים כֹּ֔ה נֶ֥גֶד אַחַ֖י וְאַחֶ֑יךָ וְיוֹכִ֖יחוּ בֵּ֥ין שְׁנֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten the rams of your flock.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob had lived with Laban for twenty years.
Jacob cared for Laban’s sheep and goats.
None of Laban’s sheep or goats miscarried while Jacob watched them.
Jacob did not eat any of the rams from Laban’s flock.
passages.original: זֶה֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים שָׁנָ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ רְחֵלֶ֥יךָ וְעִזֶּ֖יךָ לֹ֣א שִׁכֵּ֑לוּ וְאֵילֵ֥י צֹאנְךָ֖ לֹ֥א אָכָֽלְתִּי׃

passages.text: I did not bring you anything torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for what was stolen by day or night.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob worked as a shepherd for Laban.
Jacob said, “I did not bring you animals torn by wild beasts.
If an animal was lost, I took the loss myself.
You demanded that I pay for anything stolen during the day.
You also demanded that I pay for anything stolen at night.”
passages.original: טְרֵפָה֙ לֹא־ הֵבֵ֣אתִי אֵלֶ֔יךָ אָנֹכִ֣י אֲחַטֶּ֔נָּה מִיָּדִ֖י תְּבַקְשֶׁ֑נָּה גְּנֻֽבְתִ֣י י֔וֹם וּגְנֻֽבְתִ֖י לָֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: As it was, the heat consumed me by day and the frost by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob worked for Laban.
Jacob suffered in the daytime.
The heat burned Jacob during the day.
Jacob suffered at night.
The frost chilled Jacob at night.
Jacob could not sleep.
Sleep left Jacob’s eyes.
passages.original: הָיִ֧יתִי בַיּ֛וֹם אֲכָלַ֥נִי חֹ֖רֶב וְקֶ֣רַח בַּלָּ֑יְלָה וַתִּדַּ֥ד שְׁנָתִ֖י מֵֽעֵינָֽי׃

passages.text: Thus for twenty years I have served in your household—fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks—and you have changed my wages ten times!
passages.sermon:
Jacob is speaking to Laban.
Jacob served Laban for twenty years.
Jacob worked fourteen years for Laban’s two daughters.
Jacob worked six years for Laban’s flocks.
Laban changed Jacob’s wages ten times.
passages.original: זֶה־ לִּ֞י עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָה֮ בְּבֵיתֶךָ֒ עֲבַדְתִּ֜יךָ אַרְבַּֽע־ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ בִּשְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים בְּצֹאנֶ֑ךָ וַתַּחֲלֵ֥ף אֶת־ מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּ֖י עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת מֹנִֽים׃

passages.text: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, surely by now you would have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands, and last night He rendered judgment.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob said, “God was with me.
God is the God of my father.
God is the God of Abraham.
God is the Fear of Isaac.
If God had not been with me, you would have sent me away with nothing.
God saw my suffering.
God saw the hard work of my hands.
Last night, God judged between us.”
passages.original: לוּלֵ֡י אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִי֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם וּפַ֤חַד יִצְחָק֙ הָ֣יָה לִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה רֵיקָ֣ם שִׁלַּחְתָּ֑נִי אֶת־ עָנְיִ֞י וְאֶת־ יְגִ֧יעַ כַּפַּ֛י רָאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַיּ֥וֹכַח אָֽמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: But Laban answered Jacob, “These daughters are my daughters, these sons are my sons, and these flocks are my flocks! Everything you see is mine! Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine or the children they have borne?
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban said, “These daughters are my daughters.
These sons are my sons.
These flocks are my flocks.
Everything you see belongs to me.
But today I cannot do anything about my daughters.
I cannot do anything about the children they have borne.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן לָבָ֜ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַבָּנ֨וֹת בְּנֹתַ֜י וְהַבָּנִ֤ים בָּנַי֙ וְהַצֹּ֣אן צֹאנִ֔י וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לִי־ ה֑וּא וְלִבְנֹתַ֞י מָֽה־ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֤ה לָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ הַיּ֔וֹם א֥וֹ לִבְנֵיהֶ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between you and me.”
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban said, “Come now.
Let us make a covenant.
You and I will make this agreement together.
This covenant will be a witness.
It will stand between you and me.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה לְכָ֛ה נִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית אֲנִ֣י וָאָ֑תָּה וְהָיָ֥ה לְעֵ֖ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: So Jacob picked out a stone and set it up as a pillar, and he said to his relatives, “Gather some stones.” So they took stones and made a mound, and there by the mound they ate.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
Jacob took a stone.
He set up the stone as a pillar.
Jacob spoke to his relatives.
He told them, “Gather some stones.”
Jacob’s relatives gathered stones.
They took the stones.
They made a mound with the stones.
They ate there by the mound.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֥ח יַעֲקֹ֖ב אָ֑בֶן וַיְרִימֶ֖הָ מַצֵּבָֽה׃ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֤ב לְאֶחָיו֙ לִקְט֣וּ אֲבָנִ֔ים וַיִּקְח֥וּ אֲבָנִ֖ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־ גָ֑ל וַיֹּ֥אכְלוּ שָׁ֖ם עַל־ הַגָּֽל׃

passages.text: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.
passages.sermon:
Laban gave the mound a name.
Laban called the mound Jegar-sahadutha.
Jacob also gave the mound a name.
Jacob called the mound Galeed.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָא־ ל֣וֹ לָבָ֔ן יְגַ֖ר שָׂהֲדוּתָ֑א וְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב קָ֥רָא ל֖וֹ גַּלְעֵֽד׃

passages.text: Then Laban declared, “This mound is a witness between you and me this day.” Therefore the place was called Galeed.
passages.sermon:
Laban was Jacob’s father-in-law.
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban pointed to the mound of stones.
Laban said, “This mound is a witness between you and me today.”
They named the place Galeed because of this.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֔ן הַגַּ֨ל הַזֶּ֥ה עֵ֛ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינְךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם עַל־ כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־ שְׁמ֖וֹ גַּלְעֵֽד׃

passages.text: It was also called Mizpah, because Laban said, “May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban gave the place a name.
He called it Mizpah.
Laban explained the meaning of this name.
He said, “May the LORD keep watch between you and me.
Sometimes we are apart from each other.
No one else is with us.
The LORD sees us when we are not together.”
passages.original: וְהַמִּצְפָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔ר יִ֥צֶף יְהוָ֖ה בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ כִּ֥י נִסָּתֵ֖ר אִ֥ישׁ מֵרֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: If you mistreat my daughters or take other wives, although no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me.”
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban was the father of Jacob’s wives.
Laban said, “If you mistreat my daughters, God will see it.
If you take other wives besides my daughters, God will know.
No other person is here with us now.
But God is a witness between you and me.”
passages.original: אִם־ תְּעַנֶּ֣ה אֶת־ בְּנֹתַ֗י וְאִם־ תִּקַּ֤ח נָשִׁים֙ עַל־ בְּנֹתַ֔י אֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ עִמָּ֑נוּ רְאֵ֕ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים עֵ֖ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Laban also said to Jacob, “Here is the mound, and here is the pillar I have set up between you and me.
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban pointed to a mound of stones.
Laban also pointed to a pillar.
Laban said, “This is the mound.
This is the pillar.
I have set up this mound and this pillar.
I placed them between you and me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב הִנֵּ֣ה׀ הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֗ה וְהִנֵּה֙ הַמַצֵּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָרִ֖יתִי בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: This mound is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this mound to harm you, and you will not go past this mound and pillar to harm me.
passages.sermon:
Laban and Jacob made an agreement.
They set up a mound and a pillar between them.
The mound is a witness.
The pillar is a witness.
I will not cross this mound to harm you.
You will not cross this mound and this pillar to harm me.
passages.original: עֵ֚ד הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה וְעֵדָ֖ה הַמַּצֵּבָ֑ה אִם־ אָ֗נִי לֹֽא־ אֶֽעֱבֹ֤ר אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־ הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה וְאִם־ אַ֠תָּה לֹא־ תַעֲבֹ֨ר אֵלַ֜י אֶת־ הַגַּ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה וְאֶת־ הַמַּצֵּבָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לְרָעָֽה׃

passages.text: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban mentioned God.
Laban said, “May the God of Abraham judge between us.
May the God of Nahor judge between us.
May the God of their father judge between us.”
Jacob listened to Laban.
Jacob made a promise.
Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
passages.original: אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י נָחוֹר֙ יִשְׁפְּט֣וּ בֵינֵ֔ינוּ אֱלֹהֵ֖י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּפַ֖חַד אָבִ֥יו יִצְחָֽק׃

passages.text: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal. And after they had eaten, they spent the night on the mountain.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a patriarch of Israel.
Jacob stood on the mountain.
Jacob offered a sacrifice there.
Jacob called his relatives to join him.
Jacob invited them to eat a meal with him.
They ate the meal together.
They stayed overnight on the mountain.
passages.original: וַיִּזְבַּ֨ח יַעֲקֹ֥ב זֶ֙בַח֙ בָּהָ֔ר וַיִּקְרָ֥א לְאֶחָ֖יו לֶאֱכָל־ לָ֑חֶם וַיֹּ֣אכְלוּ לֶ֔חֶם וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ בָּהָֽר׃

passages.text: Early the next morning, Laban got up and kissed his grandchildren and daughters and blessed them. Then he left to return home.
passages.sermon:
Laban was the father of Jacob’s wives and the grandfather of Jacob’s children.
Laban got up early in the morning.
Laban kissed his grandchildren.
Laban kissed his daughters.
Laban blessed them.
Laban left.
Laban returned to his home.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם לָבָ֜ן בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיְנַשֵּׁ֧ק לְבָנָ֛יו וְלִבְנוֹתָ֖יו וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶתְהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ וַיָּ֥שָׁב לָבָ֖ן לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃
